postTitle: Cash Flow Forecasting: Will You Have Enough?
topic: A monthly average hides the months that come up short

assumptions.notes: Net pay €5,000 a month. Regular costs €4,000 a month. Once a year costs: car insurance €1,800 (Jan), tax top up €1,300 (Mar), summer holiday €1,200 (Jun), back to school €1,100 (Sep), holidays €1,500 (Dec). Lumps total €6,900. Year total €54,900, average €4,575 a month. Real saving €5,100 a year, €425 a month. Months above pay: Jan (€800 short), Mar (€300), Jun (€200), Sep (€100), Dec (€500). Twelfth rule: €6,900 ÷ 12 = €575 a month, so every month costs €4,575, under €5,000. Illustrative.

hookVariants.narration: Jiri saves a thousand euros a month. On paper. Five months of his year say otherwise.
onscreenLines: Five of these months say no

hookVariants.narration: Your budget works on average. The trouble is, you do not live on average. You live in January.
Many cash problems are not budgeting problems. They are calendar problems.

beats.narration: Jiri gets five thousand a month after tax. His regular costs are four thousand.
But some costs come once a year. Car insurance in January. A tax top up in March.
A summer holiday in June. Back to school in September. The holidays in December.
In five months, his costs are higher than his pay. January alone is eight hundred euros short.
Over the whole year, he saves about four hundred and twenty five a month. Not a thousand.
One common fix is the twelfth rule. Add up the once a year costs, divide by twelve, and set that aside every month.
beats.subtext: Once a year costs ÷ 12, every month

beats.narration: For Jiri, that is five hundred and seventy five a month. Once the pot has built up, every month costs the same, and none of them is short.
beats.subtext: Once the pot fills, no short months

cta.narration: Save this before your next once a year bill.

caption.instagram:
Jiri saves a thousand euros a month. On paper. Five months of his year say otherwise.

His pay is €5,000 and his regular costs are €4,000. But car insurance, a tax top up, a summer holiday, back to school and the holidays all land in single months. In five of them, he spends more than he earns. Over the year he really saves about €425 a month, not €1,000.

One common fix is the twelfth rule: add up the once a year costs, divide by 12, and set that amount aside in a separate pot every month. For Jiri, €575. Once the pot has built up, no month runs short.
